cohort: The study included 18 patients with opioid use disorder (OUD) and chronic prenatal opioid exposure who delivered at an academic hospital between January 2020 and August 2021.
finding: Following the implementation of an opioid-sparing protocol, postpartum opioid prescribing was low for patients with chronic prenatal opioid exposure, though over one-third reported poor pain control immediately postpartum and one week post-discharge.
mod_finding: No patients with a vaginal birth received an opioid prescription, half of those with a cesarean birth received one at discharge, and pain scores were higher for cesarean versus vaginal birth.
